PATH
IT services (mass recruiters)
shrinking door

Shrinking door: most fresher seats in India, but fewer each year and pay flat since 2008

DOOR SIZE, PEOPLE A YEAR
1 lakh

Sum of five companies' own FY26 statements (TCS 44,000 trainees, Infosys 20,000, Cognizant 20,000, HCLTech 11,000, Wipro 7,500), rounded down; the industry took about 4 lakh freshers in FY22 and an estimated 1.6 lakh in FY24, so the door has roughly halved in four years and Wipro has no FY27 target at all.

FRESHER PAY, LPA
3.1 to 4.5

TCS and Infosys base offers are around Rs 3.1 to 3.4 lakh and have not moved since about 2008; specialist tracks (Infosys DSE, TCS Digital and Prime, Cognizant GenC Next, Accenture AASE) pay roughly double for a small share who clear a harder coding test.

Required = employers filter on it; preferred = raises the offer probability. Each links to free-first learning with a proof of done.

Is it realistic from your college?
TIER 1

Yes, but most tier-1 graduates treat these offers as a floor; the specialist tracks (Rs 7 to 9 lakh) are where tier-1 candidates actually join.

TIER 2

Yes; this is the core catchment. Campus drives still visit well-known state and private colleges, though intake per college has fallen and offer-to-joining gaps of 6 to 12 months are common.

TIER 3

Yes, this remains the most realistic first job for a tier-3 graduate, through open tests (TCS NQT, Infosys off-campus, Cognizant GenC, Accenture ASE, Capgemini, Mphasis) rather than campus visits. What substitutes for the brand: a 60%+ academic record with no backlogs, a clear aptitude and basic coding test score, spoken English good enough for a client call, and one small deployed project. Be honest with yourself that seats are fewer each year (five firms' net headcount fell in FY26, demand.top5_it.net_headcount.fy26) and only 35% of IT employers intended to hire freshers in ISR 2026 (supply.isr2026.it_fresher_hiring_intent).

What employers screen for now
60% or 6.0 CGPA throughout (10th, 12th, degree) with no active backlogs; most mass recruiters hard-filter on this
Aptitude plus basic programming test (TCS NQT, Infosys InfyTQ-style, Cognizant GenC, Wipro NLTH, Accenture cognitive and coding assessment): arrays, strings, SQL queries, simple OOP in Java or Python
Spoken and written English at a level that passes a communication round; Accenture and Cognizant test this explicitly
One programming language to working level (Java or Python) plus SQL; for specialist tracks, LeetCode-easy DSA and a second language
Willingness to sign a service agreement and accept any base location and any project (banking, insurance, retail, telecom support are the usual first postings)
Increasingly: a certificate in cloud (AWS or Azure fundamentals) or a GenAI foundations badge; TCS reports 312,000 AI/ML-proficient staff (demand.tcs.ai_ml_proficient.q1fy27) and expects trainees to start at that baseline
Eligibility often limited to the current and previous two batches (2024 to 2026), so apply in the graduation year

Order-to-cash reconciliation service for a retail chain

Scope. A service that ingests daily sales files from 20 synthetic stores (POS CSV exports), payment-gateway settlement files and bank statements, matches them, flags mismatches with reasons, exposes a REST API and a small dashboard, and lets a finance user ask questions about exceptions in plain language via an LLM tool that only queries the reconciled tables. Includes automated tests, a nightly scheduled run and a runbook.

Domain. retail

How you use agents to build it. A coding agent generates the CSV parsers, test fixtures and the first version of the matching rules; the graduate specifies the matching logic in writing first, reviews every generated function against it, and keeps a changelog of the agent's mistakes (wrong date handling, missed partial settlements). The LLM query feature is built with strict read-only SQL and a small eval set of 30 finance questions.

Done looks like. Runs end to end nightly on a free-tier VM; matches 98% of synthetic transactions correctly with every mismatch labelled; the finance chat answers 25 of 30 eval questions correctly and refuses out-of-scope requests; README explains the business process (order, invoice, settlement, bank credit), the rules and the failure cases.

How it is verified. Test suite in CI with a published coverage number; a seeded set of 50 known mismatches that the system must catch every run; a 30-minute walkthrough the graduate can give covering the retail cash cycle, one rule that was wrong and how it was found, and why the LLM is restricted to read-only queries; a reviewer from finance or a faculty member signs off on five outputs.

Level-1 application support: read the ticket, follow the runbook, escalate	Agents triage, summarise and resolve routine tickets; TCS says its delivery model, not layoffs, changed and it expects fewer trainees per unit of work	Level-2 root-cause work, changes that touch the client's data, and talking to the client
Write CRUD screens and reports to a specification	Copilots draft the code; the trainee is expected to review, test and integrate, and to know the domain well enough to spot a wrong assumption	Requirement clarification, domain rules, code review and accountability for production
Migrate code between versions or platforms by hand (legacy modernisation)	Agents do bulk translation; large modernisation deals still need people to verify behaviour and fix edge cases	Verification design, edge-case handling, and cutover planning
Prepare status reports, documentation and meeting notes	Generated automatically from tickets and calls	Deciding what matters, negotiating scope, and client relationships; communication skills now count for more, not less

How the matcher scores this path

Base score 7 of 10 for door size this year, then these rules against your answers.

IF YOU ANSWERED	SCORE	BECAUSE
Computer Science / AI / Data Science	+1	Accepted everywhere; your competition here is every other branch, so aim for the specialist track.
Electronics and Communication	+1	Mass recruiters take ECE at the same rate as CS if you pass the coding test.
Mechanical / Automobile / Mechatronics	+1	Mass recruiters still take Mechanical and Electrical graduates when core jobs are scarce; the test does not depend on your branch.
Any other college; few or no companies visit campus	+2	This is the path where a tier-3 college matters least: open tests like TCS NQT and Infosys off-campus do not look at your college.
Well-known state or private college; companies visit campus every year (NIRF roughly 50 to 200)	+1	Campus drives still visit tier-2 colleges, though with fewer seats than before.
IIT, NIT, IIIT, BITS or a top state university (NIRF top 50)	-1	You will likely get this offer, but treat it as a floor; better doors are open to you.
Already graduated	+1	Most drives accept the previous two batches, so an already-graduated candidate can still apply through 2026.
2026	+1	The 2026 batch is in the eligibility window for every current drive.
Anywhere in India	+2	Offers come with a base location you do not choose; accepting any city is often the difference between an offer and none.
Only near home	-3	Mass recruiters post you where the project is; refusing relocation usually means the offer lapses.
0 to 3 months; I need income soon	+1	This is the fastest route to a salary for most graduates, even though joining dates can slip.
More than a year	-1	With a year of runway you can afford to aim at a better-paying door first and keep this as fallback.
Building software and apps	+1	Day-to-day work is software delivery, mostly maintenance and support at the start.
People, selling, organising, business	+1	Client communication and coordination matter more as routine coding is automated.
Research, theory and deep study	-2	There is little research or theory in entry-level services work.
A job and income as soon as possible	+3	The largest number of fresher seats and the shortest time to a first salary.
Stability and job security	-1	Intake is falling and five firms' net headcount shrank in FY26; the first job is real but not a long-term guarantee.
High pay and fast growth, even with risk	-3	Base pay has been about Rs 3 lakh for nearly two decades; growth is slow unless you move to a specialist track or out.
DSA / coding practice (LeetCode, competitive programming)	+1	Coding practice lifts you from the base track to the specialist track, which roughly doubles pay.

ABOUT
Why NextRung exists, and how it is kept honest

India produces about 8 lakh engineering degree holders a year. The IT services door that absorbed 4 lakh of them in FY22 took 1.6 lakh in FY24 and is still shrinking, and AI agents now do the routine work that was the first rung. At least 6 lakh graduates a year need a direction that is not "join an IT services company", and a way to prove they are ready for it.

How it works

Ten questions build a profile. A rules engine, not a language model, scores nine paths: a base score for how many fresher seats the door has this year, plus fit rules written by people and shown on every path page. Each path names the skills employers screen for. Your standing is the share of those skills you have evidence for, compared against the requirements in fresher postings seen this quarter. The gap becomes a 90-day plan with free-first learning and a proof of done per skill.

Four agent skills maintain the content: one refreshes the statistics from primary sources and refuses to emit a number without a URL; one maintains the path records; one maintains the skills taxonomy and learning options (every link opened before it is listed); one ingests fresher postings and maps their requirements to skills. Changes arrive as pull requests that maintainers review.

Your data

Answers stay in your browser until you sign in. With an account, your answers, ranking, evidence links and plan are stored so you can come back. Sign-in is a one-time code by email; there is no password. Your page is private unless you switch it to public, and a public page never shows your email. You can delete everything from your standing page.

What it is not

Not a job board, a course, or a guarantee. Projections are labelled projections. Where two credible sources disagree, both are shown. Where no number exists, the site says so instead of inventing one.

Contribute

The data, matcher, skills taxonomy, job mappings and this site are open source. Fix a number with a source, add an employer with a recent page, challenge a fit rule, add a learning option that is free and good, or translate a path into Hindi, Tamil, Telugu or Kannada. Placement officers, hiring managers and recent graduates are the reviewers this needs most.

Version 0.2.0, September 2026. Built to be argued with.
